project.name: dnsmasq
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `_work/src/dnsmasq` is on commit `96f6444958c29a670f4254722d787f328153605c`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. The line anchors below were resolved against this staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the `hash_questions -> extract_name` path that produced the saved ASan crash.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42506975 (dnsmasq): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_util [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42506975
bug_description.normalized: In the staged `fuzz_util` harness, lines 21-22 consume the first 150 bytes of the exact 2972-byte `poc` into `t1` and `t2`; `t2` is a 76-byte heap string (75 attacker bytes plus a NUL terminator). The caller then passes the remaining 2822 bytes and `t2` to `hash_questions(data, size, t2)`. In project code, `hash_questions` reads a nonzero `qdcount` from those bytes and calls `extract_name` with `name == t2`. `extract_name` aliases `cp` to that caller buffer, accumulates decoded output with `namelen += l + 1`, and checks only `MAXDNAME` and packet bounds. In the exact witness, bytes 154-155 are `0x20 0x20`, and the question-name bytes consumed from offsets 162-239 are also `0x20`, so the decoder sees a nonzero question count and repeated 32-byte ordinary labels. After two labels and dots plus 10 bytes of a third label, `cp` reaches the end of the 76-byte heap object; the next `*cp++ = c` at `rfc1035.c:106` writes one byte past it. The overflowed region is the fuzz target's own `t2` buffer, so the crash is grounded in `extract_name` assuming a much larger destination than the staged harness provides.

source.description: First project-code statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled DNS packet bytes: it decodes the question count from the packet header and makes the question-decoding loop execute.
source.value_from: At the call site, `header == data` points to byte 150 of the exact staged `poc` because lines 21-22 in `fuzz_util.c` each consumed 75 bytes. Bytes 154-155 are `0x20 0x20`, so `ntohs(header->qdcount)` reads `0x2020` (`8224`) and `q != 0` holds.
source.note: This is the scored source because the fuzzer entry point is unscored; line 107 is the first project statement that reads the attacker-controlled packet into vulnerability-relevant state.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The label-copy loop stores the current label byte through `cp` after earlier successful copies and dot appends have advanced `cp` to the end of the 76-byte `t2` buffer.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `WRITE of size 1` at `dnsmasq/src/rfc1035.c:106:11`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 76-byte region allocated by `get_null_terminated`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `extract_name` accepts each decoded label as long as the presentation-name total stays below `MAXDNAME` and the source packet has `l` bytes left; it never checks the actual capacity of caller buffer `name`.
root_cause.note: In the exact witness, the first three label-length bytes at offsets 162, 195, and 228 are `0x20`, and the third-label data byte that triggers the overflow is also still `0x20` at offset 239. Those ordinary 32-byte labels make `namelen` advance to 33, 66, 99, and so on. The values remain below `MAXDNAME == 1025`, and the packet prefix consumed on this path satisfies `CHECK_LEN`, so the function keeps writing into `name == t2` even after the 76-byte heap object is full.

parser_admitted.description: The saved crash proves execution remains inside the `if (succ == 0)` body. `init_daemon` only mutates local copies of its `data,size` parameters and never writes them back, so the caller-visible consumption before this gate is only the two 75-byte extractions at lines 21-22. For the exact 2972-byte `poc`, that leaves `size == 2822`, so the `size > sizeof(struct dns_header)` gate is satisfied.

tainted_value_origin.description: Earliest staging step that couples the remaining attacker-controlled packet bytes with the undersized destination buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: `t2` is the second `gb_get_null_terminated` result and refers to the 76-byte heap object allocated by `get_null_terminated`. After lines 21-22 consume 150 bytes from the exact 2972-byte `poc`, the caller's `data,size` point to the remaining 2822 bytes starting at offset 150.
tainted_value_origin.note: This call site is where the staged harness supplies `hash_questions` with both the packet bytes that drive decoding and the too-small `name` buffer that later overflows.

coarse_trace.summary: The staged harness consumes the first 150 bytes of the exact `poc` into `t1` and the 76-byte heap buffer `t2`, then passes the remaining 2822 bytes plus `t2` to `hash_questions`.
The project parser reads a nonzero question count from the packet header and enters `extract_name` to decode a DNS question name into caller buffer `name`, which still aliases `t2`.
The decoder aliases `cp` to `t2`, accepts repeated 32-byte labels under a `MAXDNAME`/packet-length guard that ignores the 76-byte destination extent, and the line-106 store writes one byte past `t2`.

fine_trace.note: The harness consumes the first 150 bytes of the exact 2972-byte `poc` into two fixed-size strings. `t2` is the second allocation: `get_null_terminated` gives it `STR_SIZE + 1` bytes with `STR_SIZE == 75`, so it is the 76-byte heap object later reported by ASan. After these two calls, the caller's `data,size` point to the remaining 2822 bytes at offset 150.
With `size == 2822`, the gate passes and the harness hands the remaining bytes to `hash_questions` as a DNS packet while reusing the 76-byte `t2` heap object as the `name` output buffer.
Source. The first project-side packet read decodes the DNS question count. In the exact witness, bytes 154-155 are `0x20 0x20`, so `q` becomes `8224` and the first question iteration executes.

At `extract_name` entry, the caller-supplied destination `name` is still `t2`, so `cp` aliases the start of the 76-byte heap buffer. The caller cursor `*pp` points at the first question-name byte immediately after the DNS header, and `isExtract == 1` initializes the destination and enables writes through `cp`.

The decoder reads the next packet byte as a label length and classifies it. In the exact witness, the first name byte at offset 162 is `0x20`, so `l == 32` and `label_type == 0x00`; parsing stays in the ordinary label-copy branch instead of terminating or following a compression pointer.

Each accepted label adds its `l` copied bytes plus one trailing dot to the decoded presentation length. In the exact witness, the first three label lengths at offsets 162, 195, and 228 are all `0x20`, so `namelen` reaches 33, 66, and 99. All of those values are below `MAXDNAME`, and the packet prefix consumed through the crashing third-label byte still satisfies `CHECK_LEN`, so the function never rejects the much smaller 76-byte destination buffer.

Sink. `cp` started at `name == t2`. Two successful 32-byte labels plus their dot appends advance it to offset 66; ten more writes from the third 32-byte label fill offsets 66-75. The next line-106 store uses `cp == t2 + 76` and writes the 1-byte overflow that ASan reports at the first byte past the 76-byte allocation.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: ASan identifies the overflowed object as the 76-byte `t2` heap buffer allocated by `get_null_terminated`; the root cause is the later `extract_name` check that limits decoded output by `MAXDNAME` and source-packet length instead of the actual caller-supplied buffer extent.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` edit unrelated DHCPv6 code in `src/rfc3315.c` and do not touch `fuzz_util.c`, `hash-questions.c`, or `rfc1035.c`, so they do not substantiate a fix for the witnessed crash.

poc.trigger: The exact staged 2972-byte witness in `poc` reproduces an AddressSanitizer 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow in `dnsmasq/src/rfc1035.c:106`. In the staged harness, lines 21-22 consume the first 150 bytes into `t1` and the 76-byte `t2` buffer, leaving 2822 bytes that `hash_questions(data, size, t2)` treats as a DNS packet. In the saved witness, bytes 154-155 are `0x20 0x20`, and the question-name bytes consumed from offsets 162-239 are `0x20`, so `extract_name` accepts repeated 32-byte labels until the line-106 store writes one byte past `t2`.

format.name: dnsmasq fuzz_util testcase
format.contract: The available evidence establishes only the exact staged 2972-byte file `poc` under the staged `fuzz_util` harness. In source, lines 21-22 each consume 75 bytes, leaving the remaining 2822 bytes at offset 150 as the packet passed to `hash_questions(data, size, t2)`. The crash-relevant bytes proven by the staged witness are narrower: `qdcount` at offsets 154-155 is `0x20 0x20`, and the question-name prefix actually consumed before the overflow spans offsets 162-239 and is `0x20` throughout. That specific harness-mediated prefix makes the decoded labels 32 bytes long and overruns the harness's own 76-byte `t2` buffer in `extract_name`; the file first diverges from `0x20` later at offset 389. The artifacts do not justify broader dnsmasq network inputs, broader numeric ranges, or any claim that the untouched remainder of the file is uniformly `0x20`, because only this exact witness and the bytes it consumes on the crashing path are observed.
